findings.notes: The wildcard glob matcher used a recursive algorithm whose running time could grow exponentially with pattern length, so a crafted policy or resource string could stall policy evaluation. Fixed by replacing it with a linear two-pointer matcher bounded by a per-call work budget, plus length caps on wildcard fields at policy admission.

Variable substitution re-scanned already-substituted text, so nested or self-referential values could drive unbounded re-scanning. Fixed by bounding substitution to the author's own template spans, with alias-hop and total-substitution limits. The substitution mitigation was completed on this line in v1.18.0-n4k.nirmata.7 by two further changes: a per-document output-size cap that also accounts whole-leaf "{ var }" substitutions, and a rewrite that resolves each substitution pass in linear time, closing a worst case where a policy whose substituted output stayed under the size cap could still consume the admission webhook's time budget.

An unchecked type assertion to string on a substituted or admission-supplied value could panic the engine or the policy-validation webhook. Fixed by guarding those assertions and degrading to an explicit error or a stringified fallback.

An unchecked type assertion in the In and NotIn operators could panic on a non-string key element. Fixed by routing In-family comparison through a shared element primitive that handles non-string elements safely.
